column1: # *** THE TAYLOR BAPTISM SERIES AT NORTHAM, read 8 October 2026 on findmypast. ***
# Devon Baptisms (findmypast, in partnership with the South West Heritage Trust and transcribed by
# volunteers of the Devon Family History Society). *** Archive reference 1843A/PR/1/16 *** - Northam,
# St Margaret. The two Bideford entries below are reference 799A/PR/1/9 and are NOT this family.
# *** FOUND BY THE MOTHER, NOT THE CHILD. *** A search on surname TAYLOR with mother's first name
# "MARY ANN HELEN" returns the whole sibling group in one page. Searching child by child would have
# taken seven searches and would not have proved the group was complete.
# *** AND THE CONTROL CAME FIRST: *** Agnes Walker Taylor, the one child whose birth this archive had
# at an exact date and address (3 August 1889, 2 Fore Street), was searched before anything else.
# She is there. So the collection covers this parish in this period and the search works.
child

column1: *** HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR ***
column5: *** BAPTISED TWO YEARS LATE, and that is the clue to the series. *** He was born at Bideford and baptised at Northam - so the family moved between, and he was done after the move.

column1: *** ISABELLA TEMPLE TAYLOR ***
column5: The second daughter - *** and the "EDIE" of 1935 ***, as this archive established the same day from four other files. The name TEMPLE is her Scottish great-grandmother's surname.

column1: *** MARGARET HELEN WALKER TAYLOR ***
column5: *** THE "W" IS SETTLED. *** The 1891 census transcription reads "Margaret H. N."; the birth index reads "Margaret Hellen W". The register says *** WALKER *** in full - the other Scottish surname, five generations up.

column1: *** IRENE TAYLOR ***
*** LUCY ELIZABETH TAYLOR ***
column5: *** PROMPT - a few weeks. *** And she is the last child before the gap that the whole Edith argument lives in.

column1: *** MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR ***
column5: *** HER OWN BAPTISM, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER HAD IT. *** Six weeks after birth. It is the first time her parents are named together in a PARISH REGISTER rather than in a tree, a census or an index - and the first record of her own that pre-dates her 1911 marriage at the Cape.

column1: *** AGNES WALKER TAYLOR ***
column5: *** EIGHTEEN DAYS. *** The control for the whole search, and the youngest of the family.

column1: # ---- *** AND THE TWO WHO ARE NOT IN IT, WHICH IS THE POINT ---- ***
# *** NO EDITH. *** Not at Northam, not to these parents, not anywhere in Devon Baptisms.
# The whole of Devon holds SIX Edith Taylors baptised c.1880-1885 and *** two of them are at Bideford ***:
#   *** EDITH TAYLOR, baptised 21 November 1883, Bideford - father William, mother MARIA ***
#   *** EDITH MARY TAYLOR, baptised 8 April 1885, Bideford - father William, mother ELIZABETH ***
# Neither mother is Mary Ann Helen or Mary Ann Ellen. *** Both are other William Taylors. ***
# *** WHAT THE GAP LOOKS LIKE. *** Lucy is baptised 31 August 1881 and Mary Septima 30 October 1884:
# *** three years and two months with no Taylor baptism in this register. *** The candidate child,
# TAYLOR Edith, Bideford, September quarter 1882, falls exactly inside it - and every sibling on
# either side of her is in the book.
# *** WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE. *** A child can be born and die before baptism; a child can be
# baptised in another parish or another denomination; a register can have a gap. *** But this family
# baptised promptly and baptised at Northam, seven times across fifteen years, and the one child the
# count requires is the one child who is not there. ***
